memories.text: HTTP 5xx regression immediately after canary deploy. Scaling had no effect. Roll back the affected service to the previous stable version and verify error rate.
Database too many connections and high p99 latency indicate connection pool exhaustion. Raise db_pool_size to 80, then restart the affected worker.
Cache timeout cascade reduced checkout availability. Repoint checkout-cache to the healthy redis cluster v2 replica.
Traffic spike saturated CPU utilization and latency. Scale capacity to 8 units and temporarily throttle traffic to 75 percent.
Retry storm amplified request rate after an upstream blip. Scaling alone intensified retries; throttle traffic to 60 percent.
Gradual memory leak reached OOM pressure and process crashes. Restart the affected worker to recover while paging the owning team for a permanent fix.
Validation error spike followed the express checkout config flag change. Revert express_checkout_enabled to false.
Orders datastore primary became unavailable and writes failed. Fail over checkout-orders to orders-db-replica.
Upstream payment provider authorization outage blocked orders. Fail over payment-provider to the secondary and throttle traffic to 50 percent during recovery.
HTTP 5xx briefly rose right after a canary deploy but the rollout was healthy; a transient upstream 5xx storm cleared on its own without a rollback.

High p99 latency and slow database responses resembled connection pool exhaustion but were caused by a missing index on a hot table; the pool itself stayed healthy and db_pool_size was already adequate.
Cache timeout errors rose from a client-side timeout misconfiguration rather than a cascade; the redis cluster v2 nodes were healthy so repointing the cache would not have helped.
A traffic spike and rising CPU with climbing latency looked like saturation but came from a runaway batch job; latency recovered once the job was killed, so scaling capacity was unnecessary.
A retry storm signature appeared in the logs but the actual request rate stayed normal; an upstream blip resolved itself and throttling traffic was not required.
Memory pressure and OOM-like process crashes on the worker traced to an oversized cache preload rather than a gradual leak; a config memory cap fixed it and a restart alone would recur.
A validation error spike followed a deploy that also flipped several config flags at once; the express checkout flag change was unrelated and reverting it would not clear the errors.
The orders datastore primary showed high write latency and slow commits under load but stayed available and kept accepting writes; failing over to the replica was not warranted.
The upstream payment provider returned intermittent authorization failures caused by a client clock skew, not a provider outage; the primary provider was healthy so failing over would not help.
Expired TLS certificate caused ingress handshake failures. Rotate the certificate and reload the edge proxy.
DNS negative caching delayed discovery after a record migration. Flush resolver caches and lower TTL.
Disk pressure on analytics workers blocked temporary file creation. Expand the volume and clean old artifacts.
Kafka consumer lag rose after a partition rebalance. Restore consumers and verify offsets advance.
Email delivery queue accumulated after SMTP rate limiting. Reduce batch size and drain the queue.
Search indexing lag followed a bulk import. Pause ingestion and allow index workers to catch up.
Authentication failures followed signing key rotation. Refresh the JWKS cache across API gateways.
Backup jobs exceeded their window because snapshots overlapped. Reschedule compaction and retry backup.
Websocket clients disconnected after idle timeout reduction. Restore the timeout and reconnect clients.
Image processing jobs failed on malformed metadata. Quarantine the bad object and replay the queue.
Recommendation quality dropped after a model feature rollout. Disable the feature and rebuild embeddings.
Audit export was delayed by object storage permissions. Restore the writer role and replay the export.
